claims.source_fact: U.S. and OECD evidence documents rising concentration in superstar firms and a decoupling between productivity and median compensation.
claims.research_inference: The United States is a strong desktop candidate for K02/K03 widening propagating imperfectly to labor income.

claims.source_fact: The Federal Reserve DFA shows the bottom half held only 1.1% of aggregate corporate equities and mutual fund shares in Q1 2026.
claims.research_inference: When equity returns are strong, concentrated ownership can amplify wealth K even if aggregate household metrics improve.

claims.source_fact: S&P evidence shows historically high top-10 concentration, while the equal-weight index is a live index only from 2003 and pre-launch history is back-tested.
claims.research_inference: U.S. index-versus-median divergence is plausible, but any replay before 2003 must avoid laundering equal-weight backtests into PIT evidence.

claims.source_fact: German collective-bargaining coverage declined markedly from 1990 to 2015, while OECD work treats wage-setting institutions as relevant to productivity-to-wage pass-through.
claims.research_inference: Germany is useful for testing whether institutional structure changes the slope from production K to household K rather than eliminating production divergence itself.

claims.source_fact: The displayed DAX return series outperformed the broader Regulated Market All Share in recent periods.
claims.research_inference: This is only a D-A candidate because global revenue exposure and sector composition can mimic a domestic K signal; classify this confounder under HN7 SECTOR_ROTATION/global exposure.

claims.source_fact: BOJ research reports that productivity rose from the late 1990s while real wages were broadly flat, with wage rigidity and employment-stability norms contributing.
claims.research_inference: Japan is a Gold candidate for D-B because aggregate/productivity recovery can coexist with weak diffusion to typical wages.

claims.source_fact: BOJ cited small-firm operating profit per employee falling from 40% of large firms in 1990 to 13% in 2024.
claims.research_inference: The widening large-small firm profit-per-worker gap makes Japan a strong D-C candidate, subject to exact vintage reconstruction.

claims.source_fact: TOPIX Large70 underperformed TOPIX over both one-year and three-year windows to 31 October 2025.
claims.research_inference: Firm K does not imply large-cap outperformance in every market window; H7 must remain conditional on valuation, sector mix, rates and liquidity.

claims.source_fact: Top Korean business groups led exports but represented only 2.7% of employment in 2017; SMEs employ most workers and have much lower productivity than large firms.
claims.research_inference: Korea is a strong desktop Gold candidate for Winner-Less-Hiring, while later SME catch-up prevents a permanent one-way K classification.

claims.source_fact: OECD reports 2013-2024 SME productivity growth of 3.7% annually versus 0.8% for large firms in Korea.
claims.research_inference: Korea provides an HN8/possible KR5 rediffusion signal: a historically wide firm-size gap can narrow at the margin even when the level remains large.

claims.source_fact: The STOXX South Korea 200 outperformed the South Korea Total Market in 2025 and in the displayed 2026 YTD/one-year windows.
claims.research_inference: Korea is a D-A candidate, but relative large-cohort performance alone cannot distinguish K capture from sector beta, valuation or semiconductor-cycle effects.

claims.source_fact: In 2025 GDP grew 5.0% and labour productivity 6.1%, while national median disposable income grew 4.4%, urban median income 3.7% and real per-capita consumption 4.4%.
claims.research_inference: China shows a current D-B candidate best described as weaker diffusion of incremental productivity to median households, not as a claim that household income failed to grow.

claims.source_fact: Official industrial data show very large recent profit-growth differences across sectors, including strong electronics profit growth and contractions in multiple traditional industries.
claims.research_inference: This supports a current industry/profit K candidate, but it does not by itself prove firm-level top-decile profit concentration or employment non-diffusion.

claims.source_fact: The World Bank China Gini series fell from 37.1 in 2020 to 35.7 in 2021 and was 36.0 in 2022.
claims.research_inference: A non-monotonic income Gini path is a hard negative against equating K-shaped structural divergence with a mechanically rising Gini coefficient.

claims.source_fact: ALFRED exposes historical real-time periods and OECD publishes snapshots of originally released short-term statistics.
claims.research_inference: A material subset of macro evidence for US and OECD-covered countries appears technically reconstructable at historical T0, but exact series coverage must be audited by G2 before replay admission.
